utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. If there are no preliminaries, then could the witness be -- next witness to be called and that would be ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: It's Thorbjorn Overgard, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And as he is being brought in, if I might just put the adjudicated facts on the record. The Prosecution has not offered certain evidence and has redacted the proffered testimony in reliance on adjudicated facts 2531, 2540, 2541, and 2858. And I neglected to say, good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, good morning to you as well, Ms. Hochhauser. That's on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Would you please put on your earphones.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Mr. Overgard. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make the solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, please, be seated, Mr. Overgard. Mr. Overgard, you'll first be examined by Ms. Hochhauser. Ms. Hochhauser is counsel for the Prosecution. And you'll find her to your right.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Good morning, Major Overgard.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, you have previously provided statements to the officer -- excuse me, to the Office of the Prosecutor, one of which was signed on 30 April 1996 and one on 1 October 1998; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And you also testified before this Tribunal in the cases against Dragomir Milosevic, Momcilo Perisic, and Radovan Karadzic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Have you had the -- have you had the opportunity prior to coming to court today to review selections of the -- of your transcript from the testimony -- your testimony in Dragomir Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. If I could ask, please, to have 65 ter 28741 on the monitor. And, sir, while that is coming up I'm just going to remind you and for myself as well because we're both speaking in the same language we have to make an effort to pause between the question and the answer.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. Now when you reviewed the relevant selections of testimony, did you find them both accurate and truthful?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And if asked the same questions today as you were then, would you give substantively the same responses?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And did you have any clarifications or corrections that you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No. That's fine. I'm fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender 65 ter 28741 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28741 receives number P1047, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might read a brief public summary of the witness's written testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Major Overgard was posted to Sarajevo as a United Nations Military Observer beginning in late October 1994. After an initial posting in an area held by the Bosnian Serb forces, he was then deployed to Hrasnica within the territory held by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which -- where he remained until the 1st of May, 1995. During his time in Hrasnica, Major Overgard investigated the death of approximately 30 to 40 civilians as a result of sniping and shelling. In each instance that he is aware of VRS held territory was identified as the source of fire. All of the sniping and the majority of the shelling incidents investigated by Major Overgard involved civilian victims. Specifically, Major Overgard investigated the G10 shelling incident of 7 April 1995 in which a modified air bomb hit a residential area in the centre of Hrasnica and killed a female civilian and wounded others. The investigation in this incident determined that the air bomb was fired from Serb-held territory in Ilidza. Serb forces from Ilidza also regularly shelled and sniped at civilians using the road to Mount Igman or the bridge at Butmir. And, Your Honours, that concludes the summary of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, Major Overgard, as you know, the Chamber is fully familiar with the selection of the previous testimony that's now been entered into evidence which you have reviewed, so I'm just going to be asking you a few follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And can we please have Exhibit P582 which is -- I guess I shouldn't called it an exhibit. P582, which has been marked for identification, on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And this is the special report from SI 1 entitled: Large explosion in Hrasnica on 7 April 1995. And if we could please turn to page 2 in the English but remain on 1 in the B/C/S. Sir, do you see your signature on this document on the monitor in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's a MO 839.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And does the -- are you -- excuse me. Are you familiar with this document and its contents and the investigation that it discusses of the explosion in Hrasnica on 7 April 1995?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, on page 2 in English where we are it reads, "The UNMOs" -- it's the -- it's what appears to be -- it's a handwritten document but it -- it's what appears to be the second paragraph: "The UNMOs heard the WPN coming," which, and you can correct me if I'm wrong, I would read as weapon, "... coming. It landed approximately," it says says "approx," but I'll read that as approximately, "200 metres from the team Loc," which, again, correct me if I'm wrong, I read as location, "but did not see it in flight." Did you personally see or hear this weapon coming in and can you describe for the Chamber what you saw or heard?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We were -- I was situated in living-room of our accommodation when we heard it coming in. It was just like big aircraft coming. We were -- it was unusual sound so we were on our way to the floor to lay down when it exploded. We didn't see anything, just heard it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And if we could turn for a moment to page 3 in the English in this document and 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'll just ask you to take a moment -- the B/C/S doesn't show the diagram. It just translates. But if you could take a moment and look at the diagram as we see it on the right-hand side of your screen.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- and this is marked as Annex A. Can you tell us is this -- is this diagram based on your own observations?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It was made by Captain Calum Gunn, the team leader at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And were you present when it was -- when it was made?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we can turn for a moment to page 4 in the English and 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And this is marked as Annex B of the document. Can you tell us who drew these diagrams and what the source of the information was to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: The source is witnesses from Mount Igman. I can only say witnesses. I cannot point if they were civilians or BiH or whatever. But this was how they discharged weapon, looked, and also where it came from -- truck on Ilidza side beside the factory building over there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And there's a -- you've described the weapon and a truck. Can you tell us, there's a third -- there's third drawing to the right of what appears to be the weapon that's marked as the aircraft bomb. Can you tell us what that represents?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It's -- it's the bomb seen from behind and we had rockets around it for a small roundings there. It's rockets and a bomb in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could turn, please, to page 5 in the English and I'm going to ask if we can just go -- show pages 5, 6, 7, and 8 in a sequence so that the witness can see them. The corresponding translation in B/C/S would be pages 6 through 9. And these pages 5 through 8 in the English are marked as Annex C. So if we could have the next page, please. And the following.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: The information and diagrams contained in pages 5 through 8 of this document, can you tell us, please, are these based on your own personal observations or some other source?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No. These are shrapnels found by the team members and they are measured by the team. So that's why we can have the 55 millimetres and 35 millimetres, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And did you -- did you see these parts?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And when you say "the team," can be more specific?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It's the UNMO team in Hrasnica, Sierra India 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could turn, please, to page 9 in the English in e-court. The corresponding translation is 10 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now specifically as to this -- this page, page 10, do you recall this page being a part of this report?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. I recall this page, and -- but I don't remember the item itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. So just to be clear, you don't remember seeing -- actually seeing the items that were depicted but you do recall that these diagrams were [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: The diagram is okay. I have seen it, and obviously I have seen also the part, but I can't remember it today.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Was this page also prepared by members of your team?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And, finally, if we can turn to the last page of the exhibit as it is in e-court which would be English page 10 and also B/C/S page 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: This appears to be the same document as we saw at page 4 but with the addition of a to/from heard on the upper left-hand corner of the page. Have you this piece of paper before, with this to/from header

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, that one I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And are you familiar with the name of the person on top, the Captain Hansen? Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I can't remember him from Sarajevo, no. But so how he comes into this picture, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now -- so with the exception of this addition of the header on that last page, does this document accurately reflect the information that you received and your own observations of the explosion in Hrasnica on 7 April 1995?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same case as we had on page 2 so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: The whole document I'm asking about --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: -- the whole report?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, the whole report is --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would offer P582 which was previously marked for identification into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number is already assigned, Your Honours. It is MFI, so it just becomes exhibit. And it's P582, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And therefore is now admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could please have 65 ter 15364 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And this is the 7 April 1995 VRS Main Staff situation report signed by Manojlo Milovanovic. And I'll ask for page 4 in the English, please, and page 3 in the B/C/S. And if I could draw your attention more towards the bottom of the page in both documents, point number 3 which says, "In the SRK/Sarajevo-Romanija Corps area of responsibility ..." And I'll draw your attention to the beginning of that first paragraph that reads: "In the 2nd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade area of responsibility, at 0600 hours, the enemy opened fire on the Famos factory" -- I'm sorry, "the enemy opened very heavy fire on the Famos," F-a-m-o-s, "factory and the neighbourhoods of" -- I apologise because I'm going to mispronounce these, "Grlica," G-r-l-i-c-a, and V-o-j-k-o-v--i-c-i. And then it goes on, "from the direction of Gradina, Igman and Lasica." And then if we could have the next page, please. I'm sorry, page 5 in the English but it remains 3 in the B/C/S. And this is under (b) situation in the corps and I'll draw your attention to where it reads: "The enemy activity was adequately responded to whereby an air bomb, 250 kg was launched on the centre of Hrasnica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It should be the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. So it would be page 4 in the B/C/S. Now, Major, can you tell us whether, on 7 April 1995 prior to your hearing the air bomb explosion, can you tell us whether you observed any fire being directed from the centre of Hrasnica towards the Famos factory or any other location.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We did not see anything unusual that morning. It was a normal morning. Always some firing in the area of the Famos factory but nothing unusual this morning. It was what we called a quiet morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And when you say there was always some firing in the area of the Famos factory I'm asking you specifically about fire directed from the centre of Hrasnica [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] sorry, from the centre of Hrasnica out toward the Famos factory?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We did not observe anything like that, that morning.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecutor kindly turn the microphone towards her, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender 65 ter 15364 at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 15364 receives number P1048, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1048 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could please see 65 ter 10144 on the screen. Oh, I misspoke. It's 10114. Thank you. And as it is coming up, this is the forensic on-site report of 7 April 1995 drafted by the forensics and KDZ anti-terrorism department.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Major, have you had the opportunity to see this document prior to today?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. And had the opportunity to review its contents?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now does the information in this report comport with the information that you and your team gathered regarding this incident?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And with the -- and with -- in its description of the parts of the bomb that were found, does it comport with what you saw?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I would tender 65 ter 10114.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10114 receives number P1049, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1049 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes my examination of this witness. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hochhauser. Is the Defence ready to start its cross-examination, Mr. Stojanovic? Mr. Overgard, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look again at P582 in e-court. Let us look at the page 1 of the English version of this document. In the statement and in this document as well, it reads, inter alia: "At 0840 hours on the 8th of April there was a major explosion in Hrasnica village." Then it goes on to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the 7th of April. At least that's what it reads both in English and in the translation. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour. Then it goes on to say: "Due to the ban on movement, it was not possible, to date, to conduct a full investigation."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain to the Court what this "ban on movement" means?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We were told by the commander of the 4th Motorised Brigade, I don't remember his name anymore, but to go back to our accommodation. We did so, and when we arrived there, there were three soldiers at the gate to the accommodation. We went in, and when we tried to go out again, we were not allowed to -- to leave accommodation for doing investigation or visit the civilian police. We were not allowed to leave accommodation until late that evening. I think it was around 7.00, 8.00 in the evening, we were allowed to move. We went then back to -- to the site just to have a look but the darkness was coming so there was not too much that we could do at the site at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How long after you were informed about the explosion did you arrive at the scene? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It is a bit difficult today to say, but half an hour, something like that. Because we went first to the civilian police station. There was nobody. And then we went directly to -- to the site where the explosion occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you remember how long you stayed at the scene before you were told to leave by the members of the 4th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I can't say anymore accurate, but it was not very long period. Maximum 15 minutes; 10, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would I be correct if I were to say that you actually arrived before the investigation crew of the criminal police of the Security Services Centre Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. We were -- as we recall the first one into the scene after the -- after the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And were you able to get any information about why they would not allow you to do your job?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, we were not given any reason otherwise, but we were not given any reason why we had to stay in accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout that whole day, you were not permitted to leave the place of your accommodation at all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you inform your superiors at any point about the problem that you had with the command of the 4th Motorised Brigade that day?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We informed our headquarter in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did they intervene? Did they send anyone to get in touch with you?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: They came patrol from the French forces at the airport to visit us and to -- just to -- to ask us about what was -- had happened in Hrasnica. They, too, were detained in our accommodation, were not allowed to leave. They -- as I recall it, they were given the permission after a while -- I don't know how -- anymore remember how long they stayed. But they stayed for a while and then we were allowed to go back to the airport later on that -- in the afternoon. But that was strictly from accommodation and back to airport area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That day, at 1900 hours, when you again went to the scene, did you note any changes compared to the situation in the morning when you first arrived at the scene?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: There were obviously people had been around on -- on -- in the -- on the site there, but -- and the -- one body I saw inside the damaged house was removed. Also that female that died was removed. So I can't -- I cannot remember -- seeing first time either, but obviously she was there in -- in the vicinity. So -- and as the darkness was coming, 7.00 in the evening, we were not able to see too much, so we were very quick or --or, we didn't stay for a long period on -- on the site. We had to wait until the morning when the daylight came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that in the morning you did see one body. I would like you to tell the Trial Chamber what it was that you saw.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I saw two legs and with uniform trousers on and boots coming out of a pile of bricks. The legs were not moving. But at -- when I discovered that, that was the same moment as the commander came and called us to come to him and -- ordered us back to accommodation, so nothing more for me to do with that. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. And did you get the impression that this was a -- the body of a uniformed soldier?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, it was uniformed trousers and military boots.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You did not see the woman, the body of the woman, about which you received information later that she was killed or was a victim.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I cannot remember seeing her at the site, no. The information about her came later on, and we did not see her before -- the day after, at the morgue, as I remember it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You were told to leave the scene at the point when you found that body; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I will complete those questions with the following question: Was the body in the building that was demolished, or was it outside of the building that was knocked down at the time?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question right. Because the body, I could see just see the legs. I couldn't see anything else. The house was demolished. It was falling down in bricks, a pile of bricks inside the house from the roofs -- or from the walls, of course. So ... this is what I can say. The area around the site was very much damaged; damaged roofs and walls, windows, and so on. But that house especially that had been closest to the impact or the explosion was totally demolished.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that the building, the school building or -- there was a school building next to the place where the bomb exploded?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, what was inside each of these houses, I cannot remember today.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to direct your attention to P582 again that you have in front of you, where, among other things, you say in this paragraph 2 in the English version, among other things, you say: "The weapon was supposedly fired from a truck in the area of Ilidza at grid BP 817 564." And then you say: "The firing point was not observed by UNMOs." When you make a note of this kind in your report, what do you mean when you say "the firing point was not observed"?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: The -- by that, we are honest to say that this was not UNMO-confirmed observation. This has been told us by witnesses, civilian witnesses, or other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that the firing point was not observed by UNMOs, do you only think here of your own team, or do you mean other teams as well, from that area?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, other UNMO teams or UNMOs in the vicinity. If they could tell us, we will say it is UNMO confirmed, and we rely on the observation; otherwise we just say we have the information but it is not UNMO confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to recall which day? Was it on the 7th at any point in time? In the evening? Or the 15 minutes in the morning? Or on the 8th that you received information, either from the army or from the civilian, that the bomb came from Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Exactly what -- when we received that information, I cannot recall today.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you look at this document, are you able to say when it was sent out to your superiors?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It was sent a couple of days after the incident. So if it was the 9th or 8th or 9th or -- I'm not quite sure because it took some time to negotiate, first of all, to have investigation, to see these shrapnels found and to measure them, and be -- the team, four of us, worked with this the following days. So exactly when it was sent I will not say. But maybe 9th in the evening or -- or even 10th in the evening, with -- because we sent reports daily, but this report that was daily sitreps, this report was sent as a special report. I think it was delivered to the headquarter, Sarajevo, 9th or 10th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could I specifically draw your attention to the B/C/S version of the date, time, group where there seems to be a transcription or -- I couldn't call it translation error, but in the English, I see 101310 B, whereas in the B/C/S version, I see 10131 A3, which seems to be different.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I also noted that. Thank you. And this is precisely why I put this question. Because from what I understand from the B/C/S version, it seems that it could be the 3rd of April, 1995. This is what causing confusion. If I may ask the witness perhaps to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But under those circumstances why would you rely on the B/C/S version if there's a clear transcription error? But then why not ask the witness could have you a look at the date, time, group and could you tell us whether it was -- on day it was sent. That is easier than to make all kind of excursions around what apparently is the real question. Could you have a look at the date, time, group, and could you tell us what that means in terms of this report being drafted or being sent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This has been drafted the 10th of April at 1300 hours, or 1310 Bravo time. So it was delivered right after that. I think in -- it is the date, time, group of -- put on when we delivered it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, this is the very practically and concrete way of approaching this matter which seems to be caused not by any unclarity in the original but, rather, by the B/C/S version not being -- not accurately reflecting what the original says. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say, in reading the document, that UNMO did not establish where the firing point was of said modified shell and that all information about the direction of the incoming shell was received from the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina or from some other witnesses at the scene?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Exactly which sources gave us this information about the firing point, I'm not able to remember clearly today. But it is -- as we say, it is not UNMO confirmed. It came from that place. But this whole investigation supports the fact that it came from that direction, due to the fact that the windows along the route it had before exploding. The device exploded, was -- the windows were damaged -- damaged. And so it clearly was a -- you can say some traces of the -- where it came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: According to your best recollection, are you able to tell us if the shell exploded as it hit the ground or it exploded before impact?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: As I remember it today, it has to be -- there was no crater, so it has -- must have exploded in the air, just over the house; that is, when you have an explosion on the ground, you will have a crater. There was no crater. It was just demolished house and roofs, windows. So I would say today that it exploded in the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that it is more difficult for any expert to determine the incoming direction of a shell if there is no marking on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It may be a bit more difficult, but it is not impossible due to the fact that it came -- this device obviously came very low. So it -- the traces along the route it followed before explosion was clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But you did not see the trajectory yourself. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That is correct. As I explained earlier, I was in the living-room with no windows that way, that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the testimony by a soldier of the B and H army at an Igman observation post who asserted that he had seen a projectile in flight and who said that shortly before impact, the bomb opened up and that a parachute appeared at the tail?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I remember there was some talk about a parachute, but I can't remember that statement from -- from -- where it came from. And we did not find any remains of any parachute, as I remember, so ... I don't remember that one. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you permit me, I want to ask you this: Do you recall giving a statement to the Prosecution on the 8th of September, 1995, and then on the 29th of April and the 30th of April, 1996, again regarding these events?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D819 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to draw your attention to paragraph 11; page 3 of the B/C/S version. And page 3, one paragraph but last in the English version. In the statement that I have just referred to and which you confirmed giving, you said, among other things: "A member of an Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina observation post on Igman claimed that he had seen the bomb while it was flying, and he said that shortly before the bomb landed, it opened and a parachute came out of the back." Does this refresh your memory --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- because this was immediately after the event? Are you also able to tell us what was exactly going on here? What were you told and when?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I don't remember that one - I'm sorry about that - because it is was some years ago. So from this detail, I don't quite clearly remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. While we're on this page, I just wanted to ask you to look at the middle of this page where it reads amongst other things --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note we don't have the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "We entered the house which was hit by the bomb."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters do not have the reference. Mr. Stojanovic, could you be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think we are able to see it. In the English version this is the third paragraph from the top. In the B/C/S version it's the fourth paragraph. If I permit me, Your Honours, I just wanted to draw the witness's attention to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It states: "We went inside the house where the bomb had landed. It was as good as impossible to determine the direction of fire." And then you go on to say, sir: "The only technical trace to determine the direction was that in the probable direction of fire all windows were broken ..." My question is this: Why did you say then, and you're saying more or less the same thing now, that it was almost -- or practically impossible to determine the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: This -- as I said then, the only thing we had to go on was the trace with the broken windows in that -- along that street, leading directly against the confrontation line and Ilidza. That's the only thing I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will finish with this question: In view of what you found at the scene the following day, would the testimony of the B and H army soldier be correct in any way that he had seen a bomb which shortly before impact opened and that a parachute appeared at the tail?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Well, to say if he is correct or not cannot be confirmed. But we have taken this into the papers afterwards, just to review and let other know what he had seen. So other sources also, as I remember, supported his observations, but I don't recall all the details about that. So what was given in the statement in 1995, I think, is -- or 1996, is -- is -- is correct. Has to be. Because the memory, we can submit, is now 18 years ago. So I can't give any more details about the incident than given in the written statement here, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This statement, did it also -- or did you take into account also this statement about the -- the -- the shell that was fired?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I'm not understanding the questions. I'm not mixing, because this statement is given long after we did the team statement, so there's a difference in time, and then this is done in a questionnaire by a policeman visiting me afterwards, and we -- I answered -- answered him upon -- from my few notes I had left, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- Mr. Stojanovic, in your question, were you referring to the information provided by a BiH soldier, or were you referring to the statement as put on paper given by this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you just first answer my question, then that might clarify already quite a few things.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Since this witness said in his statement that the ABH soldier had claimed to have seen a flying bomb, all I wanted to hear from this witness was whether, when they took position with regard about the firing point of that bomb, did he take this testimony into account as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the reference was to the BiH soldier and not to the statement of this witness. Did you, when you were interviewed, did you -- and when you made the report at the time, did you include that information that you had received from a BiH soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember if the BiH soldier came -- or that information came to us as -- when we provided the -- or before we provided the team report or if it came to me afterwards. I cannot remember that. But if this -- I don't -- if I understand the question right, if I've -- are considering the BiH soldier's statement, we have no statement from him, as I know. It's just an information given by a soldier or other sources exactly which sources, but this led to the conclusions we have in writing. And also, as I say, they are not conclusions. They are just giving facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, you earlier said "last question," but a few others followed. Did you mean by, I'll -- did you mean to say that this is the end of your cross-examination or it was the last question before the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. I have a few more documents. Therefore, I believe I will be finished during the next session. Thank you. And if I'm not mistaken, I think this is the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was unclear from where you said "I will finish with this question." We will take a break, Witness, and we resume in approximately 20 minutes from now. Would you please be so kind as to follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, the use the opportunity for the following, and it's about the testimony of Erin Gallagher: The Chamber notes, and we hereby also put it on the record, that as suggested by informal correspondence sent to the Chamber on the 22nd of February, 2013, the parties have come to an agreement whereby the direct examination of Witness Erin Gallagher, will commence following the testimony of Witness RM513 towards the end of this week and will be limited to material related to maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is further confirmed by the Prosecution's list of exhibits to be used by the witness sent on the 25th of February, which includes only exhibits for use with the witness with respect to the map materials in question. And the remainder of her direct examination shall continue on another date, as will the cross-examination. My first question to the witness is whether what I said correctly reflects the agreed -- the parties. Yes. Let me check. Yes, whether that reflect -- this correctly reflects the agreed position of the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I -- and my apologies to you, Witness, for one more second, if you would allow me. The Chamber also notes that in a motion which was filed by the Prosecution on the 22nd of February concerning this witness, that the Prosecution seeks leave to amend Ms. Gallagher's 65 ter summary. In light of the Chamber's guidance concerning such amendments, which are to be found at transcript pages 1637 up to 1639, the Chamber considers this formal request to be moot. Mr. Overgard, it's not very polite to continue speaking when you enter the courtroom. Apologies for that. Mr. Stojanovic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have P3 in e-court, page 4. Can we please zoom in on the left-hand bottom corner. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we have a map here in front of us provided by the Prosecution which is an exhibit in this case. It shows the location of Hrasnica and Ilidza. Can you please try, if it is possible, to use this map, but we also have another map showing Hrasnica in more detail if you're not able to handle this map, to indicate the place where you and your observation post was in April of 1995. Is this a suitable map for you to do that?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would kindly then ask the usher to give you a pen so that you can mark the location where you were with your observation post.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Okay. If I'm right, I'm -- this map I haven't seen for years, or too much on. It's not a detailed. But we were located in the area which I'm now -- now blue colour. I believe --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I believe in the foot of Igman, in the first houses when you come down the hill-side. So it's more ... I'm not sure on this map. I cannot say exactly. This pen also -- so somewhere -- somewhere here in that area. But I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're also on your feet. I also missed any marking, if there is any marking. Now I see is it -- I see a different colour blue at the bottom part of the -- just below the word "Hrasnica."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see two little dots. Could you -- could you add a large O to that or OP for observation post.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. It comes -- okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's at least now we have the -- more or less the centre of Hrasnica. Can you see it, Ms. Hochhauser?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please now indicated to the best of your recollection the point of impact of that projectile? And put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, in order to have any benefit of that, we need a more detailed map, because, otherwise, we get -- I do not know whether we have a more detailed map.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps we can use the map in P3 on page 36. And it's page 31 in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That might be a better idea, although, there, perhaps part of the overview is lost. But you said it was page -- now, first, if this one is --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If this map should first be saved. But before we assign a number to it perhaps we -- we focus, first of all, a hard copy page 31 in P3. Madam Registrar, could this one be saved at least, whatever number to be assigned to it temporarily.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Page number 4, as marked by the witness of Exhibit P3, receives number D241, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. You said it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- 4. This could not be possibly be page 4 of P3. It looks more as if it is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 4 in e-court, Your Honours. And page 1 in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is page 4 in e-court, I must apologise for the comments. Yes, it's page 1 in the hard copy. That's clear. Let's perhaps work with the other page number you referred to, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Can we please have page 36 in e-court, if I'm not mistaken. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Here we have a map of the Hrasnica area. If you can assist us with this map and tell us whether you can find your bearings by looking at this map right now.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Hmm ... I'm not quite familiar with this map. If the G10 spot in the middle there is the impact site, then our location was somewhere here. I'm not sure where the so-called Famos factory is located here. So it's too long a period since I've been there and seen maps, so I'm not sure anymore of -- of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then could you please put OP beneath the circle so that, in the future, we know what this refers to.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please now tell us if you remember that, at one point, you observed a mortar unit of the ABH in the area called Kovaci in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. We once saw mortars here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you intervened and requested these mortars of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to be removed from that location.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We discovered them when coming down the so-called convoy road, down to Hrasnica, and we reported them to our headquarters. And when we -- after a while, the same afternoon, went back to see if they were there still. They were removed. They were not there anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible to see in this map the approximate position where you observed the ABH mortar unit?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I'm not sure where the convoy road, what is the convoy road here, coming down from the mountain. There are more roads than I was quite aware of was there. This was not roads we used. But ... if ... no, I cannot, because I'm not quite aware where the convoy road comes down to the village or to the houses, because it was just before we -- on the end of our -- or the starting point for the convoy road just before that, behind two houses, [indiscernible] blocks, we saw them. And -- I'm not quite sure on a map anymore, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How long before the landing of that projectile in April 1995 did you caution and warn the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina that they should remove the mortars?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: First of all, we didn't do anything else but report the mortars to our headquarters. Then we went out to see if they still were there but they were removed, so someone has -- had -- had warned them or told them to remove them. The dates is no longer clear, but I believe it was -- yeah, I can't say in days, how many days before but that was a period before. Because at the moment it was me and one Argentinian UNMO, and he -- I believe he left in that period, so I can't say in number of days anymore. I haven't reviewed that report, because that was, of course, in our daily sitrep to headquarters in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You had been asked in the previous cases about the location of the headquarters of the ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the name of the unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name of the unit, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To your recollection, where was the Command of the 4th Motorised Brigade of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We had one headquarter very close to the confrontation line. In which building I don't remember exactly anymore, but it was -- yeah, of course, when I say "close to the confrontation lines," against Ilidza, it is in the houses just before that, so exactly which house I don't remember anymore. Sorry, I cannot speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you identify on this map in front of you the approximate location of the 4th Motorised Brigade Command HQ.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, I will try. It's -- it's -- that was the blocks where the -- has to be in the area here. Around that, but that's it approximately. I can't say anything exact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just mark "4 MB" above that.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Try it like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance. I think this will suffice. In view of what you discussed before, will you agree with me that the Command of the 4th Motorised Brigade was in the residential area of Hrasnica in a civilian building?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: If there were any civilians living in the building. But, of course, it was in the village, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, what kind of building that was, where the Command was.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It was, you can say, a -- a block with apartments, which had earlier been apartments but now used for military.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you also tell us do you remember if there were any lower-ranking units, such as battalions, that were stationed in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: There was one more headquarters, yes, more in the direction of the Famos factory at the other end of Hrasnica. What -- if that was a battalion or brigade headquarter, I don't remember. I believe it was a battalion headquarter. But, again, I believe today that it was the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that exist in this map; and can you mark the location?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I cannot mark it on the map anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you also please mark the police station building where you went on that morning of the 7th of April.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, exactly again, as I -- but in this area here. I -- I don't remember exactly the building because this -- I can't remember the map anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This facility to the right of the mark that you just put and to the north from the alleged point of impact, do you recall that this facility was actually a school?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: There was school in that area. Exactly, again, which building on a map, I cannot point it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, can we now look at two clips from two films --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you -- would you like to have this one saved and do you want to tender that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Thank you. I apologise, we need this to be saved and to be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, page 36 of document P3 as marked by the witness receives number D242, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D242 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, may I take it that the previously marked map, that we don't need that any further?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think I will use it once again with the next document and the area of Kovaci that is shown on the map where the mortars were. Thank you. Now, for the record, I would just like toe say that this is 1D817. There will be no audio accompanying this footage, and it lasts one minute and three seconds. After that, I would kindly ask the witness to comment and to see if that managed to refresh his memory. Thank you. Can we now look at the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please now look at the next clip, which is 1D816. This is also a segment of 50 seconds, and we shall then comment on it together.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, for the record, I would like to say that these clips come from the footage entitled: The 4th Motorised Brigade of Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the road of war. And this footage was taken in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, my question is: When you saw this first clip, do you remember this being a gym in the Aleksa Santic school and that the second footage was the inspection of the 4th Motorised Brigade in the courtyard of the school on Aleksa Santic Street. Can you recognise any of the locations?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would object to that question on a couple of grounds. But, first off, given that these clips are both from 1992, a time-period when this witness not in Sarajevo, I think we should break down what he -- whether he recognises just the location from the first clip, which was the first question. The second question was asking whether he recognised what was happening in the clip which he couldn't possibly have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's take it one by one. Let's first -- whether the witness was there in 1995 or 1992 if the building has not change, you may recognise. I can recognise quite some buildings that are already there for 300 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I agree. That's why I ask that it be broken down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first question was the gym you saw. You don't have to confirm that it was a gym because we can see that all. Do you recognise the gym as being the gym in the school as Mr. Stojanovic asked you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot. I once had the opportunity to be in that gym, but I could not recognise it from that, from this clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But there is no reason to assume it was not the gym, is there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was a gym; but where, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you do not exclude for the possibility that it is the gym as suggested to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. Next question, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The second clip shows a review in front of the school facility, and you can see those houses behind the training area. So I'm asking you whether that would make you remember that that is the school in Hrasnica the way you remember it in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, let's take it step by step. First, when you saw this yard with people lined up, did you recognise that spot where that was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You did not. Therefore, the next question is moot. But you have no reason to believe that it's not the place as suggested by Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It can be. I just haven't seen from that angle maybe. That's an easy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you whether during the time you spent in the area of Igman and Hrasnica, you had any information that the school was used for military purposes.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I cannot say that I was. I was not familiar with that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I would like to ask you to tell us, you mentioned the blue road. You mentioned the road over Mount Igman. In 1994 and 1995, who held that area of Igman, in the military sense?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It was the BiH forces. So -- because we inspected and used that road also to patrol on Mount Igman area, from the Sierra India team in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive information about whether there were any civilian facilities there from the villages on the outskirts, outside of Hrasnica, on the slopes of Igman?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Depends what civilian facilities you're talking or meaning. There were -- I don't understand the question right. I believe the -- there were civilian houses on Igman, and there were also -- but the most of them we visited were abandoned, except for one farm where there was a military headquarter. That one also in a period was a kind of OP or place where we could stay overnight in our own small cabin, when we were patrolling on Igman. Just the position of that on maps and so on, I cannot recall today, but there -- yeah, I cannot answer the question more exact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to tell us if you remember if these were villages that were inhabited until the war with Serb inhabitants or Muslim inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I cannot remember which village had which population, or if they were Serb or Muslim. I'm not able to do that today, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In patrolling the Igman and the slopes of Igman, did you see artillery weapons deployed in this area by the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I cannot remember that we saw artillery up there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us how familiar you are with the exclusion zone of 20 kilometres, heavy weapons exclusion zone, around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, there was an exclusion zone where these weapons should not be. I did not see artillery, so more than 80, 88 millimetres, inside Hrasnica area or on Mount Igman. I saw these pieces when coming down, as we mentioned before here. This might have been 120 millimetres, but as we didn't see them close, I cannot state that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because I would again like to see in electronic -- in e-court, document 53, page 4, which we had the opportunity to see a little bit earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is now Exhibit D241. D241. Could we please zoom in on the lower left-hand corner of this map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We need some patience first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we zoom in on this part where it says "Hrasnica." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can I now please ask you to indicate on the map, if you see it, the area named Kovaci and the place where you saw these mortars that you concluded were 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, I saw it before we zoomed too much here. Okay. Convoy road comes down there, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, it has to be somewhere in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that with the letters MB, "minobacaci," mortars.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would just like to ask you to tell us if you would agree with me, to save a little bit of time, to say that in relation to Hrasnica Ilidza lies to the north-west. You can see this on the map. And if the projectile came from Ilidza, would then that be the north-west direction?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, north, north-west. Yeah. Yes, I will agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now I would like to mark and tender now this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we have now the -- the second version of this document. We started with the document as marked before, which was D241, which was MFI'd. I think -- let me see now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For an unknown reason, the marking disappeared. Could we invite the witness to again mark, and now the marking to be preserved, the position of the mortars. And, again, indicate that this was the MB.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that this one, which now contains the markings of both of the observation post and of the mortar position is the one you'd like to tender? Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document -- now D241 MFI'd, as marked by the witness, receives number D243, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And D243 --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd just like to point out I don't have an objection to the document being entered but not for -- I would like to point out that these are 1992 confrontation lines. So to the extent that we're not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that an objection to the admission, or is that a comment in relation to weight to be given to this document in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: It's not an objection to admission. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then it will be admitted. And then you may make any further observations. Madam Registrar, I see that now the second marking is gone again. But it's now saved. Yeah, it's now saved. Then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the sake of the record in the transcript it always mays MB. In the -- in the map the marking was MD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: So that should be the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And D243 is admitted into evidence. Now, Mr. Stojanovic, am I right in -- did the witness not mark on the other map, the -- the observation post as well and is there any risk that we have contradictory evidence here, the one being very vague in Hrasnica, whereas, I think the witness marked the -- let me see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we briefly have a look at D242. Now, the marking of the observation post here is not even near to where it was on the previous map, which can be explained by the scale of the previous map. I suggest that the parties sit together and that they create a map in which -- agree on where the witness marked the observation post, the other markings, including the headquarters of the 4th Mountain [sic] Brigade, and where the mortars were and to make that one document so that we do not have the contradicting evidence and that we then strike this one. If the parties could engage in discussions to do that. Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Motorised Brigade, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: -- I don't have any problem obviously agreeing with Mr. Stojanovic where the witness has marked. But I think that the bigger problem perhaps is that the witness has said a number of times that these are real approximations because he doesn't feel comfortable being able to mark on the map with any of these locations. And so I wouldn't be able to agree that those, in fact, were the locations but just that where he made marks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't invite you to agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just wanted to get rid of two maps with markings which are inconsistent and to see what was the most precise one. If you could engage in such an exercise that would be appreciated. Now, one other question. Ms. Hochhauser were you familiar with the footage shown by Mr. Stojanovic; that is, the -- the gym and the school-yard?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with it. From what I could see it came from a YouTube clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen it before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because there is a suggestion that this was the school and the school-yard in Hrasnica. And at least on the yard which was shown, some military activity was ongoing. To that extent, it could be exculpatory, and I would very much encourage the parties to see whether they can agree, even if it was 1992, which only would suggest that in 1992 such activity took place, but whether they could agree on what is shown, whether these really are the locations as suggested by Mr. Stojanovic. And I think there's an active obligation for the Prosecution to explore potential exculpatory materials as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: We will, of course, do that, Your Honour. It would be helpful if Mr. Stojanovic could provide any additional information he has about the provenance of the video other than that it's on -- other than YouTube.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Most important is to have a look at the school and at the houses around the school. That seems to be the -- unless there are two schools exactly the same in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but I would be surprised by that. But, of course, the source to be further explored might help as well. Mr. Stojanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you before we move to the next document to tell me this: The way you marked the position of the B and H army mortar units, would that be within the 20-kilometre exclusion zone, in your opinion, or not.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Of course, within.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at P1049 together, please. And can we look at the first paragraph of this document, please, where, in the report on the forensic on-site investigation drafted on the 7th of April, 1995, it is noted that most probably a modified aircraft bomb landed and that the projectile came from the south-west, the Ilidza sector. Would you agree with me in view of what we saw on the map a little bit before that this assertion from the on-scene investigation does not correspond to the actual direction where Ilidza is?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: There is something, if I don't understand it, but -- south-west or -- or west. Well, it's hard for me to tell now to agree on anything about that. As I say -- I'm a bit unfamiliar with the maps at the moment. I cannot place the team location, the OP location, and -- correctly because the map is not how I remember it. But, it is as I say [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not agree on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me cut this short. The parties are invited to consider whether Ilidza, at least the village of Ilidza - doesn't say anything more - but whether Ilidza is situated in relation to the spot marked as G10 on hard copy page 31 of P3, whether that is found to the north of north-west of that spot. It seems to be obvious, but otherwise the Chamber even might make such findings. But if the parties could agree on it, that would be preferable. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this, Witness. Now I would like to move to a topic that I would also need to question you about. I just need to put a few questions to you. That first day, on the 7th of April, you did not conduct any investigation together with the official authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Not on the 7th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When did you personally practically conduct that investigation?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We had the small, I should say, orientation tour in the evening on the 7th, and the investigation was later on the day after, when we had, I believe -- yeah, on the 8th that would be in the afternoon. And then exactly when we had this shrapnel pieces, and so on, some from the second day, some the third day, on the 9th, so which one I cannot say today. Details there is -- is no longer in my memory. So the first investigation with the BiH authorities was on the 9th in the afternoon, as I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 7th, from morning until some time -- until 7.00 p.m., you were in the area of your observation post under guard by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps it's a good time for a break, and then I can move to some other documents. I am in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said you would expected to finish in the next session, but that apparently has changed now. How much time would you still need after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think that I would need some 15 to 20 minutes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will take a break but only after the witness has left the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please look at 1D818 in e-court, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the last answers you gave me, Mr. Overgard, about the time when you came to the scene, I just wanted you to clarify something for me. In front of us we see an official report of the 7th of April, 1995, drafted by the public security station in Ilidza, the crime squad department of the criminal police department which, among other things, states, that the information about the explosion was received on the same day at 0900 hours from the duty team at the Hrasnica police station. And then it goes onto say that on the same day, they went to the scene led by the people who are mentioned there. Now this something that I'm confused about. Mention should also be made of the fact that the following UN Military Observers housed in Hrasnica were also present: Captain Gunn from Great Britain and Captain Overgard from Norway. And they say that the on-site investigation commenced on the same day at 1500 hours. So what I would like to ask you is this: Is this information accurate, or is it what you said, that the investigation was actually carried out without your being present there, on the 7th?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I remember it now because at that stage when we were there on -- in the afternoon, the two of us, yeah, I remember we were there now. We were present. So we were there, but there was not too much investigation done. It was just orientation to see the house, to see the demolition done by the bomb. It was not any analysis of what have happened. Just to get the picture, the big picture, what -- what was damaged here and so on. From that visit on the site, we started to draw the picture which we had earlier here which house had damaged roofs and which one was -- what damages were done to the houses around. That was in the afternoon, yes. I remember it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the part of your statement where you say that you were at your observation post for that whole day, the 7th of April, under guard of three members of the B and H army, is not correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, as I remember now, this -- we had a short trip just before dinner. It was a short visit to the site. Exactly we what did at the site, I don't remember. But as I can recall, it was just to -- to get a picture what was damaged because we didn't have the time in the morning to do that. After that, we had to go back to accommodation again. And I don't remember exactly the details around that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did the members of the B and H army bring you to the scene, or did you yourself leave your location?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I think -- I think the crime inspector, Hakija, came. Yeah, he came. And took us over to -- to the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During the investigation on that first day, the 7th of April, do you remember if you found fragments of the projectile that hit in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We found some -- some small piece, yes, on that -- when Captain Gunn and me were there. We found -- it was just in the entrance to the house, to the -- at the gate to the house, we found something, a small shrapnel. But that's the only thing I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek clarification of one of the previous answers. You were asked whether members of the BiH army brought you to the scene. You said, "I think the crime inspector, Hakija ..." Was he a crime inspector within the army or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was a kind of inspector from the civilian police in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the answer was not that someone of the army but someone of the civilian police took [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
