utterances.text: Yes, I believe it was him. As I can recall it was him that came to -- to our place and -- and -- and we had -- was allowed to follow him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that this police inspector could ask the soldiers who had practically been keeping you from leaving your compound to let you out and go to the scene?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: For sure, he had given -- been given the permission to take us out from -- from the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the commander," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Commander of the 4th Brigade. I don't remember his name at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I told you that that was Fikret Prevljak, does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. It does, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. One more question relating to this situation: How is it possible that after three testimonies you have completely forgotten that you were on the site on that first day?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I've forgot about that afternoon visit I have. But that's -- that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that when you visited the scene on the first day, did you notice anyone clearing up the debris and the whole area where the projectile landed?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking you this is that I would like to look at page 2 of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 2 in both versions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the middle paragraph it says, inter alia, in the middle of this paragraph, "Detailed clearing of the debris revealed" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot find the reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- the interpreters have difficulties finding the part you're reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's paragraph 4, the longest one, middle portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that where it reads, "After a thorough clean-up, another" --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it reads: "After a thorough clean-up of the debris, another part of the rocket engine and three propellant charge cases were found, and on the roof of the adjacent house, two parts of the fuse were found, most probably from an aircraft bomb."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this refresh your memory? Do you recall seeing this when you were there, on that first day, the 7th of April?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That is details I -- I can't say that I remember clearly now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I will finish with this document, which reads in its penultimate paragraph: "UN Military Observers present on the scene agreed with the opinion of the investigating team regarding the projectile type and the direction from where it was fired." My question is: Do you recall that at any point in time, on that first day, there was any discussion about this issue?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I suggest -- may I tender, in fact, 1D818.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D818 receives number D244, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D244 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Overgard, just one more question relating to this on-site investigation. Do you remember whether, on that first day or the day after, there was also the investigating judge of the court in Sarajevo with you?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. She was present, if that was -- I believe it was the second day we saw her first time. On the 8th, as I remember it, but, again, as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now look at the same document, page 3 of the English, and page 4 in B/C/S. This, Mr. Overgard, is a document that bears the title: On-site investigation report, drafted by lower court II in Sarajevo, Ilidza department, in 1995, on the 7th of April. And it says the investigating judge was present, Mrs. Jadranka Kadric, and this report notes that you, UN Military Observers, were present there, together with the investigating judge on that 7th of the April. Would this document refresh your memory that this on-site investigation took place on the 7th, not the 8th of April, when the investigating judge was there?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I have no reason to say that this report is wrong, so, for sure, it -- it is correct, then it was on the 7th she was there first time. That has to be the afternoon then, the afternoon trip, from 1500 to 1600. Sorry, but -- but this report, I believe it's -- it's okay. There's no reason to believe that it is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Then let me ask you, following that answer, would you change that part of the statement where you said about your activities on the 8th on the site?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Well, then I -- I have to do that, I believe, and say that she was present already, the 7th in the afternoon. I don't remember it, so exact first time she was present, it was chaos. A lot of things happened. We were detained and we were negotiate with the -- with the commander and then also inform headquarters and so on. We had the French there, so we had a lot of things happening. So -- maybe I mix up things a bit, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I observe that in the original in B/C/S, there may be written the name of Jadranka Kadric, but it is nearly illegible. The name is missing in the English translation. Just for the sake of the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Thank you for that suggestion. I would then ask to see the next page in B/C/S, where we can see it better. And let me ask for the record to focus on the lower part where we see the name of the judge, the signature, and the stamp of the investigation court. I think, here, we can see a little better that it is, indeed, Jasminka Kadric, investigative judge. Thank you, Your Honour, for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, let me ask you one more thing on this subject and then I'll finish with it. Does it remain in your memory that in the cases in which you testify before, you also stood by your statement that you were present at the on-site investigation with the rest of the team and the investigating judge on the 8th of April, not as you stated today. Do you remember your prior testimony in different cases?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I can remember that I have given statements, but the details in the statement, sorry, there's a long time since I was in court last time, so I've gone through them but not in detail. So there is no reason for me to say that the statements are wrong, because -- or I will say that the statement, the written things, are probably right. Just my memory today is not the best.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I completely understand. I just wanted to remove all doubt because that statement is part of the record in the Milosevic case, and I wanted to make sure which corrections you would make now. Now, you mentioned the name of Fikret Prevljak, Commander of the 4th Motorised Brigade, and since that name has been mentioned in this courtroom several times before, I'd like to ask you: Do you know, as a former Military Observer in that area, that, in that segment of the territory controlled by the BH Army, there was the entrance and the exit from the tunnel under the airport runway in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: This tunnel, they started to dig it just before I left the area. So I think I have no knowledge of it being used while I still was there. There was activity in the area. We tried to investigate what it was, but it -- I didn't know exactly or for sure what -- what it was going to be before, I think, it -- yeah, the day I left or some days after. So this tunnel was not active when I was in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You -- did you try to conduct an investigation? Were you prevented from doing so?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We were not allowed to stop at that place. The -- we had different explanations of what they were doing, but no one mentioned the tunnel, of course. But we -- we had thoughts about what it could lead to, what -- what the activity was, but we had no evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see that soil is being shipped from that area?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, we saw. Because it was close to the road we used when we were on our way to -- to -- into Sarajevo and over the airport. So we -- we saw activity and that they were digging, but we're not allowed to stop and to -- to have a closer look at it. So, at that time, we didn't know -- did not know what they were constructing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us which unit denied you access to that area? Which unit of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, I -- I cannot recall which one it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In April 1995, do you remember that it was a period of the beginning of a major BH Army offensive aimed at lifting the blockade of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: There was something, but I don't -- I don't remember the -- the details about that at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recollect at all that it was a time of intensive fighting, intensive combat linked with the BH army's attempt to break out of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: There was a lot of activity, a lot of -- a lot of things happening in April 1995, yes. In Hrasnica especially there was a lot of shooting [Realtime transcript read in error "looting"], and we reported what we saw and what we could investigate. But there -- the whole big picture we did not get before late -- or later on, what was -- what -- what was happening in total. That's -- I don't remember that we had any facts reported what -- at -- major event was going on. So on that, I cannot answer you affirmatively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Overgard, did you say, "In Hrasnica especially there was a lot of shooting," or a lot of "looting"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shooting especially. Looting was not the problem in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say shooting, do you mean shooting from both sides, both warring parties?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: They were firing from both sides. They were fire exchanging so -- but we were not allowed to the confrontation line too much, so occasionally we were on the Mount Igman road and the blue road up to the position where the French had their check-point. French forces. And we could observe exchange of fire in the front line area, and that was reported, what we saw. But that it was a major break-out going on, we were not aware, I believe, as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Overgard. Those would be all the questions that I had for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not sure whether I've already tendered this, and that is part of the last document that was admitted. I mean the document involving the investigating judge, the last one I used. It's a document already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the last document shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That was 1D818, admitted as D244, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, no need to take any further action.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any plans with the video-clips?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Maybe you would accept my proposal for it to be MFI'd and then my colleague and I would, in keeping with instructions, view it all, I mean, the entire footage from which we took those two clips regarding this facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The entire footage, the Chamber is not aware of. The Chamber has been shown only two portions of that. I suggest that we reserve a number for -- and that at this moment just the two, to the extent that it is possible, Madam Registrar, but if they are uploaded separately it might be a problem.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: First video with 65 ter number 1D817 receives number D245. And second video with the number 1D816 receives number D246, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D245 and D246 are marked for identification. And the parties are invited to provide further information and, to the extent possible, agree on location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I invite you to put further questions to the witness, Ms. Hochhauser, I have one matter I'd like to raise with the witness. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You explained to us, Witness, that the broken windows allowed you to, although not with great precision, but at least allowed you to establish more or less the direction from where the projectile came. Could you explain to us how -- how -- how broken windows could assist you in establishing the direction of the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: What caused the -- the -- the windows to -- to -- to break, has to be speed, the -- the air pressure, when it passed. I cannot explain it better. As I say, when we were inside the house and we felt that something was coming our direction, we were on our way to the floor. So it was a heavy sound. So it has to be the air pressure, and the sound of that took the windows all along the street directly against the -- the confrontation line. So that's the -- the best explanation I can give.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now let me try to understand that. From the sketch which we find at page 3 - and perhaps we could have a look at it - of P582. Could we have that on the screen, please. Now, you said the -- it was established that -- or at least it was the impression that the projectile had come from north-west. Now, we see a broken window also in southwesterly direction. I see a window just on this picture as it is shown at present. It's to the right of the point of impact, main impact. How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Because it's close to the impact area or the area where the explosion occurred. Then you will have a more -- all direction pressure, air pressure going out. So that is understandable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That -- but if you follow the -- the street, then against confrontation line and again you will see more windows that were gone, whatever, not mentioned in this report. That's a pity, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I found them also in northerly direction. I find them in northwesterly direction. I -- what made you -- I mean, I do not see any broken window, well, let's say, to the south-east, even where it is close to the point of impact. Did you not find any broken windows there?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I cannot remember. But I don't think so. If -- if it had been anything a normal in that direction that we found, we would have mentioned it. But as I can recall now, it's -- it's not -- it was not damages or -- or -- in -- in a northerly direction. So this is what we saw at that side, at that time. I cannot find new things today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To say the least, I would be surprised that if windows are broken at a distance of close to 100 metres, and I'm looking to the two Ws which I find to the -- below and to the right of the crossing --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To find broken windows there and not to find them 100 metres north with such an explosion causing considerable damage to the roofs of houses, I would be surprised if all the windows in the houses remaining would still have been intact.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. I understand your question, but I can't give you a good answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And also I do not see why the building which is just a little bit up and to the left of what you called the old school, how that would have been affected by a trajectory which is, as you said, more north-west.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just wondering what the -- how you could distinguish between windows broken through the explosion and windows broken through the air pressure caused by the projectile.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah. That's -- that's a good question. But I'm still -- as I say, I cannot -- not say anything. But we followed the road and the windows were broken further against the confrontation line. But that's the only answer I can give, and for us it was obvious that it had come from that direction. I cannot say anything else today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you followed them in the direction of the confrontation line. Do you mean beyond this -- this sketch or what is found on the sketch?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Beyond the sketch.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We have to go all the way to -- further down the street and then it will -- there are more windows broken but they were not mentioned here because we were concentrating on the nearby area of the impact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did you also check whether, more in this map, more to the upper part, whether there are broken window there as well?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, we checked around and there was no more windows outside. It was in from -- in the assumpted direction, the windows were broken. And we did not mention them too much. That's -- may be a fault at that time, but -- so I cannot give you a good answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Ms. Hochhauser, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Just to follow up, please, on what we were just discussing about the blown out windows. Can you tell us, Major, what exactly was the process that you undertook when you were talking about following this to the -- following -- when you're describing your observations up to the confrontation line. Can you tell us what exactly it was that you did and what you observed.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We partly walked, partly drove along the road and we just -- okay windows gone, windows broken, blown in, not out, so -- and, okay, that was the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And for approximately what distance did you do that toward -- from the -- from the location of the explosion to the confrontation line toward Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I cannot say today how far we went, but we went pretty close up to the confrontation line, yes, as long as we could, I believe. As I can remember, we went all the way to the confrontation line found where it started to be broken windows, and so on. But we did not mention that in the -- in the report as we can see today, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And the -- the observations that you made on that path that you walked and rode, the observations of the houses and the windows in particular, was that different in nature of what you saw on the other streets in that area or any other directions?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. This was -- first of all, we were patrolling in the area and driving these roads daily, so this was new ones that had happened that morning, not -- not the day before or earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And finally on this topic, can you tell us anything about the -- the relative height of the -- of the bomb as you heard it coming in? Did you make any observations --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, we did not know what height it was, how high it was above the house when it exploded. We have no indications or things to -- to -- to say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to go back to today's transcript at page 48, line 2. You were asked by Mr. Stojanovic: How is it possible that after three testimonies you have completely forgotten that you were on the site on that first day. And I'd like to, if we could, call up 65 ter D819. I'm sorry, 1D819, which is the statement that was referred to at times in cross-examination, I believe; your 1995 statement. And I'd like to, if we can, turn to the top of page 3 in the English, and I hope I'm correct that it's the top of page 4 in the B/C/S. It says there, if I can draw your attention to it, Major, you say that -- you say about the evening of 7 April 1995 that after being told to go back to your accommodations on 7 April: "We managed to negotiate our way out at about 7.00 that night. Gunn and me went back on sites that same evening."

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And then I'd like to read to you from the Karadzic -- the testimony of your -- the transcript much your testimony in the Karadzic trial at transcript 10034, beginning at line 18, where you were asked this question and answer: "May I draw your attention to page 3 of this same document where you say that he did not want to debate anything with you. He turned you back and then in the next paragraph you say that you somehow managed to negotiate a permission to come to the scene again around 7.00 p.m." And you answered: "Yes, I believe he was there. But the 7.00 p.m. then we -- I don't remember -- but actually I did. We were there in the afternoon but we found that we had to take further investigation the next morning. And the next morning we were also not allowed out of the house, as I remember it now." Does that -- there's additional testimony, but does that refresh your recollection as to the fact that you have in fact testified in past testimony that you returned to the scene on April 7th?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah. The problem I have to remember if it was 1500 or 7.00 in the evening. I remember clearly it was 7.00 in the evening because it was beginning to be dark.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: But, sir, you've testified to that fact before that you returned to the scene on the day of the explosion.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Major, are you -- I'd like to turn to the question for a moment of the markings that you made on the maps today. Are you able to provide reliable information about the specific locations of buildings or headquarters using the maps D242 or D241, which are the maps that you marked today?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I'm afraid not. I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. And so it's fair to say that those markings cannot be relied upon to judge distance, for example, or precise location?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That's correct. I don't remember the locations so good anymore that I can put them exact.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: On a map?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Do you recall today the approximate distances from your UNMO location to the explosion -- to the location of the explosion on 7 April 1995, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That house was 200 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And do you recall the approximate distance from your UNMO location to the BiH 4th Motorised Brigade command that you spoke about?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: As I remember, approximately between 900, 1.000 metres --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we say, you earlier said your markings are such that you could not rely upon them for distances. What you're doing now is you're asking about distances in relation to headquarters where the witness said, I was unable to locate it clearly on a map. So I'm a bit confused about whether you want to rely on the recollection of the witness for establishing distances or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think the ability to place it precisely on a map is different than somebody's recollection of approximately the distances to where they -- someplace they visited from some place they were every day. I can say that this -- that -- if he -- that -- if -- sorry. Sorry. That the witness has said that it's not -- his marking are not reliable, and I'm asking him now if he can reliably give his recollection of the approximate distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if you have a distance and you have a map, you're able to locate on that map exactly where it is, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I would suggest not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you know which street to go. If you say it's 800 metres, this street, then you can just plot that on a map. But let's hear what the witness says, but I'm slightly confused. But let's hear whether the witness -- and also on what basis he has a recollection of the distance between his observation post and the headquarters of the 4th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, if we can take that last question first. Did you -- on what -- did you have the opportunity to ever visit this brigade command?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. I was there, and -- on several occasions during my stay. There -- why I can give a distance from our accommodation to the spot -- or to the place they had the headquarter and where the explosion is what I remember from earlier statements. And also when making the picture in my head from our location to the different places, I can assume where -- how -- how far it is. But I cannot give the exact position anymore on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, Major Overgard: The locations that you've -- excuse me, the distances to these locations that are expressed in your prior testimony that we've seen that's now in evidence, the 92 ter testimony, do you -- can you affirm that -- that those are the -- that -- those are reliable estimations to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: The distances is the best I can give and -- but as I say to place things directly on a map on -- today it's very difficult for me. But the distances still using the -- what is left of the mind, is better because I can remember how it looked like when you are looking out the window what -- what houses looked like, and so on. So pictures are better than maps in the mind. In my mind and ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on the -- the information that's already contained in the 92 ter testimony, on that basis I'll conclude my examination. So I have no further questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Further Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still have a few follow-up questions. Could we again have -- first of all, if you say looking out of the window, were you talking about your accommodation?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you see from your accommodation where these headquarters were.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We can exact -- not exactly see the entrance but we can see the area from -- we used -- there was a window in the roof on the bathroom in that accommodation, and from there, we also used -- we also used that position as an OP, observation post, several times during our stay. So we were used to find how far away buildings and happenings were from that area. So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So even when you could not see the entrance, you could see the building.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, could see. Estimate where the building was. I don't remember if I saw the roof of it, but we knew the last building we saw that, from there, it is only few metres to the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'd like to take you back again to P582. Could that be shown on the screen. And could we slightly zoom in. Not too much, but ... could we zoom in a bit. Little bit more. Little bit more. And a little bit more. Could you indicate on -- on this sketch which road you said you saw more broken windows?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that to the bottom, to the left, to the right? Upwards?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I believe if we see the sketch like I see it now, it's upwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's upwards.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means from the cross-roads in the direction of what you call the IMP and the car; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, could we zoom out. A bit more. Would you agree with me that on this sketch, that is south-east rather than north-west?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Hmm. Yeah, you're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions. Have the questions by the Bench or by the re-examination, have they caused any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, only one question that stems from the questions asked by my learned friend, the Prosecutor. Can we have a look at 1D819. We need page 3 in both versions. Further cross-examination by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, can you please look at the second paragraph of this statement of yours. And in the B/C/S, it's paragraph 3. If I understand correctly you gave this statement in September 1995, which is five months after the on-site investigation. You said there as well that on the following day: "Experts came from Sarajevo. In the morning, we were first not allowed to leave our house, so we could only go on-site after lunch. We conducted the investigation together with the BH police." Now, if we look at the statement that you gave five months after your on-site investigation, do you still maintain that this part of your statement is incorrect and that all of this happened on the day that this projectile landed?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: This is more like I remember it, as we started. This investigation 1500, 1600, was something coming up, and -- of course, in something -- I don't think I was -- I was -- this was me writing it. So I believe and we have to stick with this one, because this is how I remember it. This -- this 15 to 1600 on the 7th is just stood there, and -- yes, we were there, but we mixed it and I mixed it together because we were not allowed to go to the scene before -- in the afternoon when the dark was coming. That's why we were there only a short while. This is a little bit confusing also for me, because this document just briefly went through, so no details. So but this document is the one I mean is correct, the one saying that we were allowed at 1500. I just was there, as I remember it, the judge was there in the morning. So this is all, again, it's been mixed, so ... I'm -- I'm not sure anymore. I need to -- more time to -- to -- to recollect all this -- this -- this day, two days.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since there seems -- the Judges among themselves would like to verify exactly the direction. Could we have a look at P582 again. Further Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked you, and I just repeat now what I said to see whether -- because common understanding of the evidence is important for a Chamber. I asked you in which direction you saw the more broken windows. Up, left, right, or down. And you said up. Which means -- and then I said from the cross-roads in the correction of IMP and car. Therefore, that's not to the left, not to the right, not downwards but up.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Then I was wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I then put it to you that that is southeasterly direction, rather than north-west. Let me just verify again whether this is common understanding of your testimony among myself and the colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to be sure, when you said, I saw it in that street upwards, that is further upwards where no buildings are further depicted. That is how I understood your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is -- well, let's say --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I was wrong. [Overlapping speakers] ... not marking here. I say I was wrong. Yeah, you got me there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to be quite sure, when you say that you saw more broken windows up in this road further up, upwards, in southeasterly direction is that also where your accommodation was.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: First of all, that is -- I just found that I was -- I said wrong. It should be downwards. Because if I'm right now the -- our accommodation should be in the right upper corner of this drawing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As we see it now. You say there was your accommodation --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: So if I understand this drawing right now, I have to take a position in our accommodation, and if that is up in a right-hand corner, then we should -- I should go downwards to the confrontation line, if that is right [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you mark for me where your accommodation was, looking at this map.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah. If we say [Overlapping speakers] ... I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... we'll ask you to -- so carefully consider where the location of the old school is.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That one is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is north. And could you --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: North we have here in the mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but could it not be zoomed in again and again. Could we zoom out. Yes. Is there any possibility that you could mark approximately where this -- your accommodation was? And please --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: In that direction, if I'm right. Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We see that are you now --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I'm a bit confused now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it assist you if, for example, you would be shown a -- a Google Earth or a Google Maps printout? Would you be better able to orient yourself in relation to where your accommodation was.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I hope so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps we should try to achieve that over the break and make at various scales a Google Maps impressions so as to better enable you to tell us where your accommodation was. Well, this document as now marked by the witness, should be at least MFI'd. Madam Registrar the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number C4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, would you share the property of this -- this map, marked map with the Chamber, then we would make it a D exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honours. I have no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll give it a D number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Then document receives D245 Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D245 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: May I make the suggestion that perhaps over the break Mr. Stojanovic and I together with the witness attempt to use Google Maps to locate the -- no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Oh, you'll do it. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we'll do it. You can do it. What I expect you or the Defence to do is to make a colour printout of the exact location on Google Maps or Google Earth - perhaps even better - where you see buildings, where you see -- and then ask the witness to mark that after he returns to the courtroom. We'd rather not -- the witness is expected not to communicate with the parties meanwhile. Now I don't know who has the colour printer nearest by. It's ... perhaps Prosecution. If we could have it zoomed in at various levels so that we could make a series of two or three, and then ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, in order to avoid further confusion, is it correct that 245 and 246 were assigned to the video.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, yes, that is true. Then document marked by the witness, document P54 -- yeah, receives number D247, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. We take a break and resume at -- Yes, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise, Judge. If we could have the witness put on the record the exact intersection that he is referring to as his accommodation, so that I can probably locate it on Google Maps or locate the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. What I'd like is that you focus on what is -- in the Prosecution's position, is this cross-roads. That is also clear from the map we looked at earlier, which was marked by the witness, where the name of the street appears and the impact was located at number 1 in the many reports. That location is easily, with the help of this -- if I could refer you to hard copy page 31 of the -- of the hard copy in P3 gives you sufficient clues to find it on Google Maps, I think. And what I'd like to have at various levels of zooming in, the area around what is indicated on this map as G10, which is on the -- a cross-roads at the end of Aleksa Santic Street. If that would help you and we could then compare later. To the extent possible if it could be uploaded already into e-court as a series of Google Earth maps -- or that -- if that's possible, fine. If not, we'll look at it at the -- We -- then could the witness first be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 10 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber establishes that Mr. Mladic is not in the courtroom. We were informed that Mr. Mladic, in order not to miss a visit which was scheduled for early the afternoon, has waived his right to be present. Mr. Lukic, that's what you can confirm?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Last time when you gave a form to us in which he waived his right to be present, we invited you to file that. That has never been done, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We corrected this time, and it is filed just a few moments ago. So maybe it is not in the system yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore, could the Chamber have a look at the document, even if it's a hard copy, where Mr. Mladic ... We'll continue in the absence of Mr. Mladic. Could we have -- first of all, could we have the witness escorted into the courtroom. And, at the same time, could we have page 36 of P3, which is the Hrasnica map, on our screens. I'm looking with full expectation to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: By some feat of technological genius, which was not mine, we have two images, one closer up and one further out. On colour paper we have not been able to upload them or anything like that, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we could have a look at them then perhaps I would like to distribute to the parties a series of four which gives even a better context. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I gave a few more Google Earth prints to the -- the parties in order to -- to allow them to orient themselves. The first one is with -- on top the airport, and to the bottom it is Hrasnica. You see there is a kind of a cross-roads with a sharp angle which we also find on the picture which is on our screen at this moment. Do we all agree that this is a Hrasnica and we verified the Prosecution's copy, which depicts the same, although in colour now. Parties all agree that it is adequate -- adequately reflecting the relevant area.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then what -- yes. Now, what I suggest is the following: That we first try to agree on where approximately the impact is. And, for that purpose, could the first coloured map produced by the Prosecution be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only two copies that I was able to produce are in Your Honours' hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll give them -- in order to be put on the ELMO. This one first. And, Witness, could I invite you, first of all, to carefully look at this moment at the map you have before you, and which was shown to you earlier in which you marked. And could I especially ask your attention for the Aleksa Santica Street, which runs south-east to north-west on this map, just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you still have the picture of page 36? Can you see the -- which is not a Google Earth yet but is still the map.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you see there a street called Aleksa Santica, which runs from south-east up to where G10 is indicated.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you to carefully try to keep this picture in your memory when we move to what is now on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's nothing on the ELMO. Is the ELMO not functioning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we are. There we are. Witness, do you now recognise, more or less, what we have on our screen? And could I -- is there ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we zoom in like that. Witness, do you still have on your mind the previous picture? We can always switch back to -- what I see is the cross-roads under the sharp angle a little bit further up. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just trying to orientate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there is a street going - and the orientation of this map is north to the top -- goes in approximately southwesterly direction.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where there is a cross-roads, four roads crossing, but the crossing is of irregular shape. Do you see that? It's not ...

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Then down here ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The problem is we can't follow you in your --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- I'll try to guide you again. At the top part, we have a road which arrives from almost northerly direction and ends in a kind of a huge roundabout. You see that?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now you turn down -- you go down from that roundabout in southerly direction a little south-east -- south-west. I apologise for. You see that?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, from that roundabout south to southwesterly direction, and then you arrive at what looks like cross-roads but is not the regular cross-roads but is a funny-shaped kind of a place where the four streets coming together.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I'm addressing the parties: Is it that cross-road which is indicated on the map as G10? Is that the cross-road where the impact is located? That is just to the east of that -- immediately east to that cross-roads.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it is a little bit to that one side but, yes, that is the cross-road that I believe is

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] that's the cross-road. Mr. Stojanovic, you agree as well. Now, can we -- Witness, my next question is: If that is the cross-roads where the impact is, can you orient yourself?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You believe so.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That was a bit difficult, but ... I can see that -- the place where you have the G10. I believe I have the -- the right position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: But from there, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, are you able to tell us, taken from that position, where your accommodation was?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Accommodation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to -- to -- perhaps to assist you, you see at the -- up, left part of this picture, you see bigger buildings which seems to be residential flats. I don't know whether they are, but that's what at the look like, just for your orientation. What we see from the cross-roads in more or less northerly direction there are some larger buildings which, if we look at the map we saw a minute ago, is an area where a street is called Skolska which sounds very much like school road, but I'm not a B/C/S-speaking person. Now, could we move up again a bit slightly the -- or at least it -- move down so that we have a bigger area. Yes. Perhaps a little bit further up again. Yes. Now, have you had an opportunity to -- not to be zoomed in. Looking at all this Witness, are you now able to orient yourself in such a way that you could more or less tell us where your accommodation was?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Not immediately. I'm not able. Because there were some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is, of course, how it looks today.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. There was some ditches and also a little bit road on both sites of the ditches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But could you tell us in what direction it was. Is it from this cross-road, is it purely south, is it south-west?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: South -- south of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of the cross-roads?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means the road leading to the bottom --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of this picture.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The bottom of this picture, a little bit to the left, which bends before it reaches the bottom of the picture.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the parties agree that that is -- from G10 that it is southeasterly direction or I should say south to south-east close to south slightly east.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, that I would agree to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would say approximately -- at approximately 200 degrees on the compass; 180 being purely south and 270 being west.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Judge, I can agree that it is south and then it curves slight, to the -- to the left. It goes slightly to left --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would be on that road if would be on the left. If you look at the picture, it is to the right. Then we have a different ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, is this clear to you as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. While preparing for this, we tried to find the location so we do have an idea of where that could be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which would mean that if you would travel from your accommodation to the cross-roads where we have identified G10 to be, that you would travel in northerly just west of northerly direction.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do all parties agree on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: To be frank, Your Honour, I'm getting a little confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'll do the following: Could the -- could the -- could we first look at the second one. Here we see the same cross-roads. Do you see that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could you by hand, mark, first of all, and put a circle around the cross-roads. And you need an ordinary pen for that, or can you do it on the screen. I don't know whether it's possible. I don't think so because we're not in e-court. We should -- should be done on paper with a marker, a clear -- yes. Could it be put on the -- it -- it is on the ELMO. Could an ordinary pen be given to the witness. If there's a marker that would even be clearer. Yes. Now, Witness, I would now like to invite you to make a marking not on the screen but on the paper. Could you first put a circle around the cross-roads you think G10 was -- was being depicted.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That would be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear. Could we put again. Now, could you tell us in which direction from this, by indicating it by an arrow, in which direction your accommodation was.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It is down. That has to be down that road and down in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] houses here I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: There are two houses if it is this one. Or that one. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you put around the two houses a circle and add the letter A for accommodation.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My final question: There's no doubt in your mind that it was along this road that your accommodation was. That is, southerly direction.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Not 100 per cent, no. Because it is new buildings, new roads here. That wasn't there at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but to the best of your recollection --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which means that your accommodation was south from the point of impact. I suggest that this will be uploaded into e-court but be given to Madam Registrar first and that we assign a -- preferably perhaps a D number, Mr. Stojanovic, to this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Hard copy document marked by the witness receives number D248, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D248. Any objection? D248 is admitted into evidence and should be uploaded into e-court. Now a last question to you, Witness: You said -- you indicated that it was due to the fact that the windows were shaking where you were, which you explained as the consequence of speed of a projectile flying over your head, that this made you conclude that the windows broken you saw, that that must have been the trajectory of the projectile. Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You also agree with me that if the projectile flew over your head on the assumption that you have well marked the direction where your accommodation was, that it had not come from northwesterly direction, but, rather from southeasterly direction. Because this map was oriented north up --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as is the other map which still may be on your screen at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah. No name on that road. Because on the sketch I was wrong when I then said go upwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that map was -- that map was oriented in a different way. As a matter of fact, what you indicated as being upwards was south -- south-east.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah. That is not -- not correct. It was opposite direction. Downwards on -- on the sketch. Has to be so. That was the sketch that was confusing me a bit, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that you saw the broken windows on a road arriving from your accommodation to where G10 is to the road to the left.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: On the road to the left of G10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which goes on this map -- and we are looking at page 36 of P3, which goes in the direction to where we have the Proleterska and Marta and Ula.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the direction that you --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I think we have tried to clarify as good as we could the whole testimony about directions. Unless the parties have any further questions in this respect? No further questions, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have any additional questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Just one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Further re-examination by Ms. Hochhauser:

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, when you described how you then walked and drove the -- the route where you -- upon -- the route where you observed the broken windows, and you said that you followed it right up the confrontation line. The confrontation line where?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Against Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber noticed that at least on the maps there are confrontation lines in both directions. South-west -- north-west and south-east. Then if there are no further questions, I'd like to thank you very much for coming --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're relieved by having ended this exercise. Mr. Overgard. Mr. Overgard, I'd like to thank you for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Hopefully we have it clarified now. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any matter to be raised by the parties urgently? If not, we'll adjourn and we resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 27th of February, 2013, in this same courtroom, I. We stand adjourned.
